steps.title: Step 0 — intro: activating prior knowledge
steps.content:
Teacher recalls with the students what they have already been taught, so the work on
cylinders, spheres and volume has something to stand on:
steps.note:
1. properties of cubes and cuboid
2. properties of pyramids and cones

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content:
Teacher displays shapes of cylinders and spheres while the students identify the
properties. Teacher draws the shapes on the board and add to the properties already
mentioned by the students if there is need.

draws the shapes on the board and adds to the properties already mentioned by the students

blocks.question:
1. How many circular faces does a solid cylinder have?
2. A cylinder has how many faces.

steps.title: Step II
steps.content:
Teacher explains how to derive the formula for volume of cube and cuboid while the
students listen and ask questions where they do not understand. They copy worked examples
into their notes, which also work the volume of a prism as area of base times height.

activities.what: explains how to derive the formula for volume of cube and cuboid, and works the volume of a prism as area of base times height
listen and ask questions where they do not understand
copy worked examples into their notes

steps.note:
#### Volume of cube and cuboid

1. Volume of cuboid = Area of base $\times$ height

   $= \text{length} \times \text{breadth} \times \text{height}$

   $= lbh$

2. Volume of cube = Length $\times$ Length $\times$ Length

   $= l^{3}$

**Example 1.** Calculate the volume of a cuboid of length 3cm, breadth 2cm and height 8cm.

Solution:

Volume of cuboid $= L \times b \times h$

length $= 3cm$

breadth $= 2cm$

height $= 8cm$

Volume $= 3cm \times 2cm \times 8cm$

$= 48cm^{3}$

**Example 2.** The volume of a cuboid is 24cm$^{3}$. If the base is 6cm by 2cm. Find the
height of the cuboid.

Solution:

Volume of cuboid $= L \times b \times h$

length $= 6cm$

breadth $= 2cm$

height $= ?$

Volume $= 24cm^{3}$

$24cm^{3} = 6cm \times 2cm \times h$

$24cm^{3} = 12cm^{2}h$

Divide both side by 12cm$^{2}$

$\frac{24cm^{3}}{12cm^{2}} = \frac{12cm^{2}h}{12cm^{2}}$

$2cm = h$

$h = 2cm$

#### Volume of cube

**Example 3.** Calculate the volume of a cube of side 3cm.

Solution

Volume of cube $= l^{3}$

$V = (3cm)^{3}$

$V = 3cm \times 3cm \times 3cm$

$V = 27cm^{3}$

#### Volume of prism

Calculate the volume of the prism below.

**fig-03.** A triangular prism lying on its rectangular face. The triangular end has a base
of 5 m and a height of 3 m, and the prism runs back 10 m.

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.42,line width=0.5pt]
  \draw (0,0) -- (5,0) -- (2.5,3) -- cycle;
  \draw (5,0) -- (8.5,1.8);
  \draw (2.5,3) -- (6,4.8);
  \draw (8.5,1.8) -- (6,4.8);
  \draw[dashed] (0,0) -- (3.5,1.8);
  \draw[dashed] (3.5,1.8) -- (8.5,1.8);
  \draw[dashed] (3.5,1.8) -- (6,4.8);
  \draw[dashed] (2.5,0) -- (2.5,3);
  \node[below] at (2.5,-0.15) {$5\,\mathrm{m}$};
  \node[left] at (2.35,1.5) {$3\,\mathrm{m}$};
  \node[below right] at (6.9,0.8) {$10\,\mathrm{m}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

Solution:

Area of triangular face $= \frac{1}{2}bh$

$= \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 3$

$= 7.5m^{2}$

Volume of prism $=$ Area of base $\times$ height

$= 7.5m^{2} \times 10m$

$= 75m^{3}$

steps.title: Evaluation
steps.content:
Teacher tests the students' understanding on the topic by giving them some questions to
solve.

Question:

1. Calculate the volume of a cuboid 8cm long, 4cm wide and 3cm high.
2. Calculate the volume of cuboid with dimensions 5m by 2m by 3m.
3. What is the volume of a cube of 4cm $\times$ 4cm $\times$ 4cm.
4. A rectangular tank hold 6m long by 2m wide holds 36m$^{3}$ of water. How deep is the
   water in the tank.
